elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 11 as rendered: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof." Only the jurisdiction words were swapped for "Arizona"; the conflict-of-laws tail is retained.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Section 19 as rendered: Disputes "will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over the merits, and each party irrevocably submits to the jurisdiction of such courts; provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, so the exclusive merits forum survives; the binding-arbitration mechanic and the award-confirmation sentence are removed and the heading conformed to "Jurisdiction," leaving no dangling arbitration reference.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects the laws of the State of New York, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is expected because the proposal targets the preferred level, which supersedes the fallback.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The forum is the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Again consistent with the preferred-level target.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: both preferred elements are met in operative language (New York governing law in Section 11; exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction over the merits in Section 19 with a carve-out confined to temporary injunctive relief).

The original clause was a genuine deviation and walk-away risk: Arizona law (outside the accepted set) plus mandatory binding arbitration under U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules with no court venue provision, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.

Minimality holds. In Section 11 only the two jurisdiction words changed, with the severability sentence and the conflict-of-laws tail intact. In Section 19 the excised text (the binding-arbitration referral, the arbitration rules citation, and the award-confirmation sentence keyed to the arbitrator) is exactly what had to go to install a court forum; the heading change from "Arbitration" to "Jurisdiction" is required to avoid a retained heading contradicting the operative text. No survival tails, fee-shifting, jury-waiver, service-of-process, or other boilerplate extras were added.

Intent is preserved: the defined term "Disputes" and its broad scope (common law, statutory, equitable; before or after the Effective Date; clauses (b) and (c) covering other agreements and dealings) are retained unchanged, and the "Except as otherwise specified below" lead-in now points to the retained temporary-injunctive-relief proviso rather than to a deleted arbitration exception, so no dangling cross-reference or undefined term results.
No action required from the drafter; the fallback is correctly offered in the margin comment as an alternative rather than being relied on in the operative text.
